findings.finding: The pin is written before the review cascade, but the plan does not specify how `shipped_head` is updated after the review-record commit is created. For a normal reviewed unit, that commit changes the branch tip; leaving `shipped_head` at the pin-time value makes the later verification fail, while updating it without tightly defining the order can reintroduce a race.
findings.suggestion: Define one explicit post-review transaction: verify `reviewed_head`, create and push the review-record commit, capture its resulting SHA, atomically update `review_pin.json` with `shipped_head`, then verify that exact SHA immediately before merge. Fail closed on any mismatch.

findings.finding: The stated “single detection path” does not actually detect a PR base change. The specified verify mode checks branch ancestry/tip against pinned SHAs, but never compares the live PR’s node ID, head ref/OID, and base ref to the values persisted in the pin. Persisting `pr_base_ref` alone is not protection.
findings.suggestion: At merge-time verification, query the PR by pinned node ID and require its current head ref/OID and base ref to match the pinned identity. Treat a missing, closed, retargeted, or head-changed PR as a failure requiring re-review/re-pin.

findings.finding: “Actual tip” is ambiguous. Checking `HEAD` in the selected worktree will not detect a manual remote push if that worktree has not fetched; it can pass against a stale local branch.
findings.suggestion: Fetch the relevant remote ref and compare the pinned SHA with `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` (and the PR’s current head OID where available), not only the local checkout. Define fetch failure as fail-closed.

findings.finding: The plan assumes a reliable `origin/{default}` and sufficient history for `merge-base`, but does not establish those prerequisites. Detached worktrees, shallow clones, renamed remotes, and unavailable remote refs will otherwise produce misleading pins or inconsistent failures.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the campaign’s canonical default-branch/remote resolver from R2 if one exists; otherwise add a small preflight that fetches the required refs and rejects unsupported/shallow-history states with a clear error.

findings.finding: The shared-worktree fallback is safe only while the legacy workflow guarantees one active unit. A partially migrated state with multiple rows lacking `worktree` can still select the shared checkout for the wrong unit—or merely fail intermittently depending on checkout timing.
findings.suggestion: Permit fallback only when the scheduler proves legacy single-unit execution; otherwise reject missing `worktree` data. Add a test for two active legacy-shaped rows to ensure it fails rather than silently attributing a diff.

findings.finding: Keeping the legacy `reviewed_head` file preserves compatibility, but the described existing conditional read (`[ -f ... ] &&`) can still permit an unpinned merge if pin creation or the dual-write fails. The acceptance criterion requires fail-closed behavior, not only a best-effort legacy file.
findings.suggestion: Make 3g require a valid pin/legacy head value and always pass it as `--match-head-commit`; no file, malformed pin, or failed verification must block merging. Test the missing-file and malformed-file paths explicitly.

findings.finding: The new pin file is shared state between review and merge steps, but the plan does not require atomic writes or define retry/idempotency behavior. A crash or concurrent retry can leave truncated JSON or a pin belonging to a previous attempt.
findings.suggestion: Write to an attempt-specific temporary file and atomically rename it; validate `unit_id` and `attempt_id` on every read. Define whether a retry replaces a pin only after confirming it refers to the same immutable review state.

findings.finding: The implementation will consume worktree paths, branch names, and PR identifiers from state and interpolate them into documented shell calls. If state is malformed or externally influenced, unquoted shell expansion can become command injection or cause Git commands to operate outside the campaign directory.
findings.suggestion: Use argument-safe invocation/quoting, validate worktree paths are expected campaign worktrees, and use the pinned PR node ID rather than branch-name parsing wherever GitHub is queried.

findings.finding: The tests focus on the guard in isolation and a simulation of the old failure, but do not prove that every real 3f-bis/3g command now uses the selected unit worktree and pinned merge SHA. Documentation-driven workflow call sites are especially prone to one stale command surviving the edit.
findings.suggestion: Add an integration-style fixture that executes the relevant workflow snippets with two worktrees and a mocked PR response, asserting the diff, payload root, review commit, push, PR lookup, and merge command all resolve to the intended unit.  Overall, unit-scoping the workflow and pinning immutable commit/PR identity is the right approach, but the merge-time verification contract needs to be completed and made fail-closed before shipping. The proposed tests should also cover the actual 3f-bis/3g integration, not only the new helper.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: `_single_parent` swallows `ReviewAttributionError` from `_run_git` and returns `None`. Both call sites pass a SHA that was just resolved by `rev-parse --verify refs/heads/...` (verify:342/376) or asserted equal to it (ship:425/442), so `rev-list` can only fail STRUCTURALLY here (git missing, timeout, corrupt object). The except turns that structural failure into an ancestry verdict: verify() returns `ok=False` with detail 'parent None vs pinned reviewed_head ...' instead of raising, and ship() reports "shipped_head X's parent None does not equal pinned reviewed_head" - an operator reads that as a merge/ancestry problem, not a git failure. Fail-closed either way, so non-blocking.
findings.suggestion: Drop the try/except in `_single_parent` and let `_run_git`'s ReviewAttributionError propagate (the CLI already maps it to exit 1 / BLOCK with the real git stderr).

findings.finding: The re-derived `pr_url` has no emptiness guard, unlike the original derivation earlier in the step (`[ -n "$pr_url" ] && [ "$pr_url" != "null" ] || STRICT-STOP`). findings.finding: Claim under doubt: 3f-bis, as written, carries a reviewed unit from pin to ship on the live path — campaign-mode.md 239-242 states the rule (state crosses steps in a FILE; a fresh Bash call has an empty environment) but 3f-bis breaks it internally. `run_dir` (243) and `pr_url` (245) are consumed at 365 (`echo "$shipped_head" > "$run_dir/reviewed_head"`) and 383 (`gh pr view "$pr_url"` / `cat "$run_dir/reviewed_head"`) AFTER three Agent-tool spawns (a/b/c) and several `record` calls -- necessarily different Bash calls. `diff_head`/`fires` (261-264) are consumed at 309/314, and `fires` requires the orchestrator to READ the diff and judge risk flags, so the pin call is realistically a separate Bash call too. Every branch is fail-closed for the merge, but the mechanism cannot complete a reviewed unit unless the orchestrator silently re-derives the variables the doc forbids relying on. No prose test covers intra-step variable lifetime (test_the_head_pin_crosses_steps_in_a_file_not_a_shell_variable only checks 3f-bis->3g).

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: a Stage-2 finding can be 'addressed' at 3f-bis without producing a misattributed merge (code-review lows (a)+(c), assessed jointly and escalated) — Line 389 ('a Stage-2 high finding left unaddressed -> STRICT-STOP') tells the orchestrator addressing is allowed; the only way to address a code finding is a fix commit F on top of reviewed_head. The step then says record `completed` rows, `git commit` R, `git push` (363, ||STRICT-STOP passes), overwrite `$run_dir/reviewed_head` with R (365), THEN `--mode ship` (374-377) -- which now refuses because R^ == F != reviewed_head. Net state after that STRICT-STOP: origin/{branch} = reviewed_head+F+R with reviews.json on it saying every stage `completed` for a diff the reviewers never saw (F is unreviewed); review_pin.json.shipped_head = null; the legacy file = R. The doc says the PR is 'left OPEN so a human can repair it' -- a human resuming at 3g runs `--match-head-commit $(cat reviewed_head)` = R and merges the mixed reviewed/unreviewed tree with a green record on it: the exact misattribution class R3 exists to close, reached by following the doc's own prose. The automated loop is safe (STRICT-STOP never reaches 3g; a re-entry hits `rm -f` at 243), which is why each half was rated low in isolation; together, on the routine Stage-2-finding path, they steer into a post-push stop with a stale, rejected legacy pin.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: ship()'s 'exactly one commit ahead of reviewed_head' check proves the shipped tree is the reviewed tree plus reviews.json (code-review low (b), escalated) — `git rev-parse {sha}^` (review_attribution.py:425, and :355 in verify) resolves the FIRST parent only, and the check is topology-only -- it never looks at what the one commit contains; the spec demoted `diff_sha256` to 'evidence, not a gate', so nothing content-level backs the sole live enforcement point. findings.finding: The updated test asserts that 3g retains the optional `[ -f "$run_dir/reviewed_head" ]` behavior, but does not test the required fail-closed merge behavior. It would pass while a missing pin still produces an unpinned merge.
findings.suggestion: Add a workflow-level test that a missing, malformed, or wrong-unit pin blocks 3g and that every merge invocation includes `--match-head-commit`.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The pin helper covers several important cases, but the actual merge path remains optional and can still merge without a pinned head. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

The spec says `--mode pin` "runs unconditionally at 3f-bis's top". The diff places the pin call *after* the `gh pr view` STRICT-STOP, the trigger computation, and the diff computation. Any unit where `gh pr view` fails (no PR, gh auth hiccup, transient API error) STRICT-STOPs the loop *before* a pin exists — and 3g's `[ -f "$run_dir/reviewed_head" ]` check then leaves `head_pin=""`, i.e. an unpinned merge window on the resume path once the PR appears. The doc's own argument ("a PR already exists by this point") covers the happy path only.
Suggestion: move the pin invocation (with `--review-skipped` when the trigger hasn't fired) above the `gh pr view` call, making PR-identity args genuinely optional/null on that path, or make 3g fail closed on a missing pin file rather than merging with `head_pin=""`.
